note: 63 NEW animation primitives for the Prism Animatable catalog (batch 2, toward 300). None duplicate the existing 90. category is one of the 15 closed unions in contract.ts. exportName = camelCase(name)+'Primitive'. Waves E/F/G of ~21 each. CONTRACT IS FROZEN — agents touch only their two new files.

E.name: flip-3d
E.label: 3D Flip
E.subject: card
E.description: Card performs a full 3D flip, rotating a complete half-turn through depth with a perspective foreshorten at the edge-on midpoint.
E.behavior: rotation.y (or .x per axis) eases 0 -> Math.PI (a full 180deg half-turn) over duration via easeInOut; at phase 0.5 (edge-on) apply a brief scale.x dip toward ~0.15 then back to 1 to read as foreshortening; opacity stays 1. DISTINCT from existing 'flip' (which is a partial 0.85*PI fade-in): this is a full continuous half-turn with a foreshorten dip. Controls: duration (fader 0.4..3), axis (dropdown x|y), curve (curve). Read axis live to pick rotation.x vs rotation.y. Observable: rotation differs t=0 vs mid; scale.x dips near mid. Restore rotation/scale in dispose.

E.name: cube-rotate
E.label: Cube Rotate
E.subject: card
E.description: Card swings in as if it were one face of a rotating cube, pivoting around a hinge offset behind it so it arcs through depth.
E.behavior: Move the card to a pivot: set object.position to a hinge point and rotate the whole object so the card (a child at +halfDepth offset, OR offset via position.z before rotation) traces a cube-face arc. Simplest deterministic impl: rotation.y eases from -Math.PI/2 to 0 while position.z eases from -depth to 0 and position.x from -depth to 0, so the face swings from the side of a cube to front-facing. Controls: duration (fader), depth (fader 0.5..3), curve (curve). Observable: rotation.y and position.z both change across phase. DISTINCT from flip/flip-3d by the simultaneous positional arc. Restore in dispose.

E.name: card-fold
E.label: Card Fold
E.subject: card
E.description: Card unfolds open from a folded-shut crease, scaling its height open from a thin horizontal strip while a slight rotation simulates the fold lifting.
E.behavior: scale.y eases 0.04 -> 1 via easeOut (unfolding from a thin creased strip); rotation.x adds a small fold-lift easing from ~0.5rad to 0; opacity rises 0->1 early. Controls: duration (fader), axis (dropdown y|x -> which scale axis folds), creaseLift (knob 0..1 scaling the rotation.x). Observable: scale.y grows; rotation.x decreases. DISTINCT from any existing (no fold primitive). Restore scale/rotation in dispose.

E.name: unfold
E.label: Unfold
E.subject: card
E.description: Card unfolds accordion-style from a narrow vertical strip to full width with a springy backOut settle.
E.behavior: scale.x eases 0.06 -> 1 via backOut (springy unfold past 1 then settle); a faint rotation.y wobble = sin(phase*PI*2)*wobbleAmp*(1-phase) damping out; opacity rises. Controls: duration (fader), wobble (knob 0..0.4 rad), overshoot fixed via backOut. Observable: scale.x grows and overshoots >1 mid-phase. DISTINCT from card-fold (x vs y, accordion vs crease) and unfold has the springy overshoot. Restore in dispose.

E.name: door-open
E.label: Door Open
E.subject: card
E.description: Card swings open like a door hinged on its left edge, rotating around that edge from shut to flat-facing the viewer.
E.behavior: Hinge the rotation on the card's left edge: in seek, translate the object so its left edge is the pivot (offset = -halfWidth on x), rotate.y from hingeClosed (~ -Math.PI*0.55, edge toward viewer) easing to 0 (flat), then translate back — net effect the card swings open around its left edge. Use a measured half-width fallback (e.g. 1.2). opacity rises early. Controls: duration (fader), hingeSide (dropdown left|right -> sign of pivot+angle), openAngleDeg (knob 60..160 start angle). Observable: rotation.y changes; the pivot offset makes position trace an arc. Restore in dispose.

E.name: zoom-rotate-in
E.label: Zoom Rotate In
E.subject: card
E.description: Card scales up from nothing while spinning a full turn, a punchy combined zoom-and-spin entrance.
E.behavior: scale (uniform) eases 0 -> 1 via backOut (slight overshoot); rotation.z eases from turns*2PI -> 0 via easeOut; opacity 0->1. Controls: duration (fader), turns (knob 0.25..2), scaleOvershoot (knob 1..1.4 multiplies the mid overshoot), direction baked. DISTINCT from rotate-in (small z angle, no full-turn spin) and zoom-blur (blur jitter). Observable: scale grows, rotation.z decreases. Restore in dispose.

E.name: depth-pop
E.label: Depth Pop
E.subject: card
E.description: Card rushes forward from deep in Z to its resting plane, scaling up with perspective as it nears.
E.behavior: position.z eases from -depth (far) to 0 via expoOut; scale tracks a perspective approximation (e.g. scale = lerp(0.3, 1, eased)); opacity 0->1. Controls: duration (fader), depth (fader 3..14), curve (curve). DISTINCT from scale-pop (pure scale) and depth-pop adds the z translate + perspective scale coupling. Observable: position.z and scale change across phase. Restore in dispose.

E.name: tumble
E.label: Tumble In
E.subject: card
E.description: Card tumbles into place, rotating on both X and Y axes at once before settling upright.
E.behavior: rotation.x eases from spinX*2PI -> 0 and rotation.y from spinY*2PI -> 0 (different counts) via easeOut; scale 0.5 -> 1; opacity rises. Controls: duration (fader), spinX (knob 0..2), spinY (knob 0..2). DISTINCT (no dual-axis tumble exists). Observable: rotation.x and rotation.y both change; verify rotation.x != rotation.y mid-phase for non-equal spin counts. Restore in dispose.

E.name: fade-up
E.label: Fade Up
E.subject: card
E.description: Card fades in while drifting gently upward into place — the classic content-reveal.
E.behavior: opacity 0->1 via easeOut; position.y eases from -rise to 0 (drifts up). Controls: duration (fader), rise (fader 0.2..3 world units), curve (curve). DISTINCT from plain 'fade' by the coupled upward translate; DISTINCT from 'slide' which is horizontal/configurable and has no fade-priority. Observable: opacity rises and position.y increases. Restore in dispose.

E.name: fade-scale
E.label: Fade Scale
E.subject: card
E.description: Card fades in while easing up from a slightly shrunken 0.9 scale to full — a soft, premium reveal.
E.behavior: opacity 0->1; scale eases from startScale (default 0.9) -> 1 via easeOut. Controls: duration (fader), startScale (fader 0.5..0.98), curve (curve). DISTINCT from scale-pop (pops from 0 with overshoot) — this is a subtle settle from near-1 coupled to a fade. Observable: opacity + scale both change. Restore in dispose.

E.name: cross-dissolve
E.label: Cross Dissolve
E.subject: card
E.description: Card cross-dissolves through a brief desaturated tint dip, like a film cross-fade between two shots.
E.behavior: opacity dips then recovers: opacity = 1 - dipDepth*sin(phase*PI) so it's full at ends and lowest at mid; simultaneously shift a found material's emissiveIntensity or color tint toward a neutral mid then back (track emissiveIntensity). Controls: duration (fader), dipDepth (fader 0.2..0.9), tint (knob 0..1 scaling the emissive dip). DISTINCT from fade-through-black (goes to black/min, monotone dip) — cross-dissolve recovers symmetrically with a tint shift. Observable: opacity at mid < at start. Restore material in dispose.

E.name: scroll-zoom
E.label: Scroll Zoom
E.subject: card
E.description: Scroll position zooms the card in and out — scrubbing scroll scales it smoothly through a focal pass.
E.behavior: Reads target.userData.scroll (0..1; fallback phase(t)). scale = lerp(minScale, maxScale, scroll) (or a focal bell: peak at scroll 0.5). Controls: minScale (fader 0.4..1), maxScale (fader 1..2.5), focal (toggle -> bell curve vs linear). Observable: scale tracks scroll. DISTINCT from scroll-rotate-3d/scrub-morph (no pure scroll-driven zoom exists). Restore in dispose.

E.name: scroll-fade-stack
E.label: Scroll Fade Stack
E.subject: card
E.description: Card fades and lifts through a scroll band — appears as it enters, recedes as it leaves, like a stacking scroll list.
E.behavior: Reads userData.scroll; opacity follows an enter/exit window [start,end]: 0 before start, ramps to 1 across the band, then optionally fades after; position.y = lerp(enterY, 0, windowed) lifting into place. Controls: start (fader 0..0.6), end (fader 0.4..1), lift (fader 0.5..4). Observable: opacity & position.y change across the scroll band. Restore in dispose.

E.name: scroll-skew
E.label: Scroll Skew
E.subject: card
E.description: Scroll velocity shears the card — fast scrolling skews it, settling back to square when scroll rests.
E.behavior: Reads userData.scroll; derive a velocity proxy = scroll - prevScroll (store prevScroll on closure across seeks); apply a shear by rotating/scaling: e.g. rotation.z = clamp(velocity*skewGain, -maxSkew, maxSkew) and a scale.y stretch proportional. When velocity ~0 it returns to square. Controls: skewGain (knob), maxSkewDeg (knob 5..45), stretch (toggle adds scale.y). Observable: changing scroll between seeks produces nonzero rotation.z; equal consecutive scroll -> ~0. Restore in dispose.

E.name: scroll-color-shift
E.label: Scroll Color Shift
E.subject: card
E.description: Scroll drives a hue/emissive shift across the card — scrolling re-lights it through a color sweep.
E.behavior: Reads userData.scroll; map scroll to a found material's emissiveIntensity = lerp(loGlow, hiGlow, scroll) and shift material.color/emissive hue around the wheel by scroll (use a Color and setHSL with h = baseH + scroll*hueRange). Track emissiveIntensity as observable. Controls: hueRange (knob 0..1), loGlow (fader 0..1), hiGlow (fader 0.5..3). Observable: emissiveIntensity tracks scroll. Restore material color/emissive in dispose.

E.name: pointer-tilt-3d
E.label: Pointer Tilt 3D
E.subject: card
E.description: Card tilts in 3D toward the pointer like a parallax trading-card, rotating on X and Y to face the cursor.
E.behavior: Reads userData.pointer {x,y} in 0..1; offset from center (-0.5..0.5); rotation.y = offsetX*maxTilt, rotation.x = -offsetY*maxTilt (lerp toward target each seek for smoothness). Optional slight position.z lift at center. Controls: maxTiltDeg (knob 5..40), smoothing (knob lerp factor 0.05..1), invert (toggle). DISTINCT from hover-lift (z+scale+emissive on proximity) and parallax-layers (children offsets) — this is whole-card 3D tilt. Observable: pointer offset produces rotation.x/.y. Restore in dispose.

E.name: spotlight-follow
E.label: Spotlight Follow
E.subject: card
E.description: A bright specular hotspot tracks the pointer across the card surface, like a light gliding over glass.
E.behavior: TSL: swap subject.material to a MeshStandardNodeMaterial (three/webgpu) whose emissiveNode adds a soft radial highlight centered at uPointer (a uniform vec2 in 0..1 uv space) — emissive += baseColor * smoothstep(radius, 0, length(uv - uPointer)) * intensity. seek reads userData.pointer and updates uPointer; also advance a faint idle drift so it's never fully static. Controls: radius (fader 0.1..0.6), intensity (knob 0..4), tint (color). Use three/tsl (uv, uniform, length, smoothstep) and CAST node assignments like caustics.ts. Track uPointer.value/uIntensity.value as observable. Restore prevMat in dispose.

E.name: stretch-text
E.label: Stretch Text
E.subject: text
E.description: Glyphs stretch tall on entrance then snap back to natural proportions with an elastic settle, one after another.
E.behavior: subject is a Group of glyph children. Per glyph i: when phase passes i/N, scale.y springs from ~2.2 down to 1 via elasticOut while scale.x compensates (squash-stretch volume feel, scale.x from ~0.6 to 1); opacity rises. Controls: duration (fader), stagger (knob 0..1 fraction), stretch (knob 1.5..3 initial scale.y). Iterate subject.children. Observable: a glyph's scale.y differs early vs late and across glyphs at a fixed t. Restore children scale in dispose.

E.name: decode-text
E.label: Decode Text
E.subject: text
E.description: Glyphs resolve out of a rapid scramble of jitter and flicker, locking into place left-to-right like a decryption reveal.
E.behavior: Per glyph i deterministic (index hash, NO Math.random): before its reveal time (i/N) the glyph rapidly jitters position (x/y offset keyed to floor(t*rate)+i hash) and flickers opacity/emissive; once phase passes its reveal threshold the jitter amplitude ramps to 0 and it locks (scale 1, opacity 1). Controls: duration (fader), rate (knob 8..40 scramble speed), intensity (knob jitter amplitude). DISTINCT from existing 'scramble' (whole-subject) and glitch-text (RGB split, decays uniformly) — decode is a left-to-right sequential lock. Observable: count of locked glyphs grows with t; a pre-reveal glyph's offset differs from its locked state. Restore in dispose.

E.name: text-blur-in
E.label: Text Blur In
E.subject: text
E.description: Glyphs resolve from a soft out-of-focus shimmer — a per-glyph blur proxy (jitter + low opacity + slight overscale) snapping to crisp, in sequence.
E.behavior: Per glyph i staggered by i/N: simulate blur with low opacity + a small deterministic multi-sample jitter on position (averaging ghost feel) + scale from ~1.3 -> 1, all resolving to crisp (jitter 0, opacity 1, scale 1) as the glyph's local phase completes. Controls: duration (fader), stagger (knob), blurAmount (knob 0.05..0.4 initial jitter+overscale). DISTINCT from text-cascade (drop) / typewriter (reveal) — this is a focus resolve. Observable: per-glyph scale/opacity change in sequence. Restore in dispose.

E.name: text-pop-each
E.label: Text Pop
E.subject: text
E.description: Each glyph pops in with a bouncy backOut overshoot, scaling from zero in quick left-to-right succession.
E.behavior: Per glyph i: local phase = clamp((phase - i*stagger)/window, 0,1); scale = backOut(localPhase) (0 -> overshoot >1 -> 1); opacity = localPhase>0?1:0 ramped. Controls: duration (fader), stagger (knob 0..0.3), overshoot (knob 1..1.8 amplitude of backOut). DISTINCT from text-extrude (z depth), text-cascade (drop+bounce position), this is pure per-glyph scale pop. Observable: glyph scale grows in sequence; scale overshoots >1 mid local phase. Restore in dispose.

F.name: split-3d
F.label: Split 3D
F.subject: text
F.description: The line splits at center and the two halves rotate in from opposite depths, swinging together like double doors closing into the headline.
F.behavior: subject is a Group of glyphs. Partition glyphs into left half (index < N/2) and right half. Each half rotates in 3D from an opposite start: left glyphs rotation.y from +halfAngle (and position.x from -spread) easing to 0; right glyphs rotation.y from -halfAngle (position.x from +spread) to 0; opacity rises. Controls: duration (fader), spread (fader 1..6 initial separation), angleDeg (knob 30..120). Iterate subject.children with index to assign half. Observable: a left-half glyph rotation.y is opposite-signed to a right-half glyph mid-phase, both -> 0. Restore in dispose.

F.name: liquid-text
F.label: Liquid Text
F.subject: text
F.description: Glyphs flow on a continuous liquid wave, bobbing and gently scaling as a wave of 'fluid' passes through the word.
F.behavior: Looping (duration Infinity). Per glyph i continuous: position.y = sin(t*speed + i*phaseStep)*amp; scale = 1 + sin(t*speed*0.7 + i*phaseStep)*scaleAmp (a viscous breathing); small rotation.z follows the wave slope. Controls: speed (knob), amplitude (fader), viscosity (knob -> phaseStep coupling neighbors). DISTINCT from wave-text (pure y sine) by the coupled scale+rotation liquid feel. Observable: glyph.position.y AND scale vary by index and time; pick two distinct t values. Restore in dispose.

F.name: text-spotlight
F.label: Text Spotlight
F.subject: text
F.description: A bright spotlight band sweeps across the line, lighting each glyph emissive as it passes, then settling to an even glow.
F.behavior: A sweep position sweep = phase (0->1, or looping). Per glyph i at normalized x = i/N: glyph material emissiveIntensity = base + peak * smoothstepBump(|x - sweep|, width) (brightest when the sweep is over it). After the pass, settle to a steady mild glow. Track one glyph material's emissiveIntensity. Controls: duration (fader), width (knob 0.05..0.5 band width), peak (knob 0..4). Iterate subject.children materials. Observable: a glyph's emissiveIntensity peaks at a specific t as the band crosses. Restore materials in dispose. Deterministic.

F.name: cloth-sway
F.label: Cloth Sway
F.subject: plane
F.description: The plane hangs and sways like draped cloth in a breeze — pinned along its top edge, billowing more toward the free bottom.
F.behavior: CPU vertex displacement on the subdivided plane (mirror wave.ts: read base positions once, write each seek, needsUpdate). For each vertex with normalized vertical v (0 top pinned, 1 bottom free): z += sin(x*freq + t*speed)*amp*v + sin(y*freq*0.6 + t*speed*1.3)*amp*0.5*v (sway grows toward the bottom). Controls: speed (knob), amplitude (fader), stiffness (knob -> how fast amp grows with v). Observable: a bottom-row vertex z differs t=0 vs mid; top-row vertex stays ~pinned. Restore base positions in dispose. DISTINCT from flag-wave (left-pinned horizontal travel).

F.name: hair-sway
F.label: Hair Sway
F.subject: plane
F.description: Fine vertical strands sway side to side like hair or grass in wind — high-frequency horizontal displacement increasing toward the free tips.
F.behavior: CPU vertex displacement: for each vertex with normalized vertical v (0 root, 1 tip): x += (sin(t*speed + y*strandFreq) + 0.4*sin(t*speed*1.7 + x*7))*amp*v*v (quadratic growth toward tips; high strandFreq makes distinct strands). Controls: speed (knob), amplitude (fader), strandFreq (knob 4..20). Observable: a tip-row vertex x differs across time; root stays. Restore base positions in dispose. DISTINCT from cloth-sway (z billow) — hair sways in-plane on x.

F.name: banner-flutter
F.label: Banner Flutter
F.subject: plane
F.description: A hanging banner flutters — a travelling vertical ripple runs down its length with gusty amplitude.
F.behavior: CPU vertex displacement: z = sin(y*freq + t*speed)*amp * gust(t) where gust(t) = 0.6 + 0.4*sin(t*0.6) (amplitude breathes like wind gusts); pinned along the top (scale amp by normalized v from top). Controls: speed (knob), amplitude (fader), gustiness (knob 0..1 scaling the gust modulation). Observable: a vertex z varies with time and the amplitude envelope changes. Restore base positions in dispose. DISTINCT from flag-wave (horizontal x-pinned travel) — banner travels vertically with gusts.

F.name: water-surface
F.label: Water Surface
F.subject: plane
F.description: A calm water surface with gentle interfering ripples — softer and slower than the choppy ocean.
F.behavior: CPU vertex displacement summing 2-3 low-amplitude long-wavelength sines from different directions: z = sum( sin(dot(dir_k,[x,y])*freq_k + t*speed_k)*amp_k ); keep amplitudes small and wavelengths long for a calm sheet. Controls: calm (knob -> inverse amplitude), speed (knob), ripple (knob freq scale). Observable: vertex z varies across time. Restore base positions in dispose. DISTINCT from ocean-fft (large Gerstner choppiness) and ripple-pool (discrete drop sources) — this is a calm continuous sheet.

F.name: wind-ripple
F.label: Wind Ripple
F.subject: plane
F.description: Gusts of wind chase ripples across the surface — bands of displacement sweep through with a moving gust front.
F.behavior: CPU vertex displacement: a gust front position g = t*frontSpeed; z = sin(x*freq + t*speed)*amp * gustBand(x, g) where gustBand = exp(-((x - wrap(g))^2)*sharpness) so a localized band of ripple sweeps across x. Controls: frontSpeed (knob), amplitude (fader), sharpness (knob 0.2..4 band tightness). Observable: vertex z changes over time; the active band moves. Restore base positions in dispose. DISTINCT — moving localized gust band, not a uniform field.

F.name: wipe-linear
F.label: Linear Wipe
F.subject: card
F.description: A hard directional wipe sweeps across the card, revealing it edge-to-edge with a crisp soft-edged front.
F.behavior: TSL: swap subject.material to a MeshStandardNodeMaterial (three/webgpu); opacityNode = smoothstep(uProgress - softness, uProgress, coord) where coord is uv.x (or chosen axis/direction) — a moving alpha front. seek advances uProgress 0->1 over phase. Use three/tsl (uv, uniform, smoothstep) and CAST node assignments like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), direction (dropdown ltr|rtl|ttb|btt -> coord & sign), softness (knob 0.0..0.4). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from iris-wipe (radial).

F.name: clock-wipe
F.label: Clock Wipe
F.subject: card
F.description: A radial clock-hand sweep reveals the card, the alpha front rotating around the center like a clock wiping the image in.
F.behavior: TSL opacityNode using angle: ang = atan(uv.y-0.5, uv.x-0.5) normalized to 0..1; opacityNode = step(ang_normalized, uProgress) (everything the hand has passed is visible). seek advances uProgress 0->1. Use three/tsl (uv, atan/atan2, uniform, step/smoothstep) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), direction (dropdown cw|ccw -> sign), startAngleDeg (knob 0..360 offset). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from iris-wipe (radius) and wipe-linear (axis).

F.name: blinds-wipe
F.label: Blinds Wipe
F.subject: card
F.description: Venetian-blind slats open in unison to reveal the card — alpha stripes that widen until the whole image shows.
F.behavior: TSL opacityNode = stripes: f = fract(uv.y * slats); opacityNode = step(f, uProgress) (each slat opens from one side as progress grows). seek advances uProgress 0->1. Use three/tsl (uv, fract, step, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), slats (knob 3..24 stripe count), orientation (dropdown horizontal|vertical -> uv.y vs uv.x). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose.

F.name: diamond-wipe
F.label: Diamond Wipe
F.subject: card
F.description: An expanding diamond opens from the center, revealing the card outward in a rotated-square mask front.
F.behavior: TSL opacityNode using Chebyshev/diamond distance: d = abs(uv.x-0.5) + abs(uv.y-0.5) (diamond) ; opacityNode = smoothstep(uProgress+softness, uProgress, d) so a growing diamond reveals outward. seek advances uProgress ~0 -> ~1. Use three/tsl (uv, abs, smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), shape (dropdown diamond|square -> L1 vs LINF distance), softness (knob). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from iris-wipe (circular L2).

F.name: motion-blur-streak
F.label: Motion Streak
F.subject: card
F.description: Card slides in with a directional motion-streak — a stretched, ghosted smear that compresses to a crisp solid as it stops.
F.behavior: Approximate motion blur without postprocessing: position.x eases from -distance to 0 (expoOut); scale.x stretches proportional to the per-seek velocity (fast = stretched, settle = 1) — compute velocity = |x - prevX| stored on closure; opacity from low (streaked) to 1. Controls: duration (fader), distance (fader), streak (knob 1..4 max stretch). DISTINCT from slide (no stretch) / zoom-blur (radial). Observable: scale.x > 1 while moving, ~1 at end; position.x changes. Restore in dispose.

F.name: defocus-pulse
F.label: Defocus Pulse
F.subject: card
F.description: Card breathes in and out of focus on a loop — a soft defocus proxy via subtle scale jitter and opacity pulse, like a lens hunting focus.
F.behavior: Looping (duration Infinity): a focus value f = 0.5+0.5*sin(t*speed); blur proxy = (1-f): scale = 1 + (1-f)*overscale (slightly larger when defocused) + tiny deterministic multi-axis jitter scaled by (1-f); opacity = lerp(minOpacity, 1, f). Controls: speed (knob), overscale (knob 0..0.3), minOpacity (fader 0.3..0.9). Observable: scale/opacity differ across two distinct t. DISTINCT from blur-in/zoom-blur (one-shot entrances). Restore in dispose.

F.name: paint-spread
F.label: Paint Spread
F.subject: card
F.description: Paint blooms across the card from the center, an organic ink-edged blot growing to fill the surface and reveal it.
F.behavior: TSL: swap subject.material to a MeshStandardNodeMaterial; opacityNode = smoothstep(uProgress, uProgress-edge, d - noise(uv*noiseScale)*wobble) where d = length(uv-0.5) — a growing radius with a noisy organic edge. seek advances uProgress 0 -> ~1.0. Use three/tsl (uv, length, a sin/fbm noise, smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), noiseScale (knob 2..12 edge raggedness), wobble (knob 0..0.4 edge irregularity). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from ink-spread (existing wave-category fluid look) — this is a center-out alpha reveal of the card itself.

F.name: splat-reveal
F.label: Splat Reveal
F.subject: card
F.description: Several paint splats burst and merge to reveal the card — multiple deterministic blobs growing and unioning into full coverage.
F.behavior: TSL opacityNode: union of K (3-5) fixed-position metaball blobs: acc = max over k of smoothstep(uProgress*radius_k, 0, length(uv - center_k)); opacityNode = smoothstep(0.5, 0.6, acc + uProgress*0.3). Blob centers are deterministic constants. seek advances uProgress 0->1 (full coverage). Use three/tsl (uv, length, max, smoothstep, uniform). Controls: duration (fader), blobs (dropdown 3|4|5 -> active count), spread (knob 0.2..0.6 blob radius). Track uProgress.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from paint-spread (single center blot).

F.name: crumble
F.label: Crumble
F.subject: card
F.description: The card crumbles into a shower of falling shards — fragments break off, tumble, and fall away under gravity.
F.behavior: CPU: like shatter, build a Group of fragment meshes (small planes/cubes) covering the card area at deterministic grid positions, hide the subject (or set subject invisible) — OR if simpler, displace the subject's geometry vertices outward+down. Preferred deterministic impl: create a grid of NxM small fragment meshes into target.object; in seek each fragment k (after a per-fragment stagger from an index hash) accelerates: position.y -= 0.5*g*localT^2, rotation tumbles, opacity fades. Controls: duration (fader), gravity (knob), fragments (knob 3..8 grid density). Deterministic (index hash). Observable: a fragment's position.y decreases over time. Restore/dispose the fragment group + restore subject visibility in dispose. DISTINCT from shatter (assemble/explode in place).

F.name: dissolve-burn
F.label: Burn Dissolve
F.subject: card
F.description: The card burns away (or in) along a glowing ember edge — a noise threshold eats the alpha with a hot emissive rim at the burn front.
F.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial; n = noise(uv*scale); opacityNode = step(uThreshold, n) (burns away as uThreshold rises) OR reverse for burn-in; emissiveNode adds a hot rim = emberColor * smoothstep(uThreshold+rim, uThreshold, n) so the dissolving edge glows. seek advances uThreshold (0->1 burn away, or 1->0 burn in per direction). Use three/tsl (uv, noise, step/smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: duration (fader), scale (knob 2..14 noise scale), direction (dropdown burn-in|burn-out -> threshold sweep direction). Track uThreshold.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from dissolve-noise (no ember rim) and pixel-dissolve (blocky).

F.name: voxelize
F.label: Voxelize
F.subject: card
F.description: The card breaks into a grid of small cubes that scatter outward then reassemble into the flat surface.
F.behavior: CPU: build a grid of NxM small cube meshes (InstancedMesh or a Group) into target.object representing the card; hide subject. In seek each voxel k has a scatter target derived from an index hash (a 3D offset + rotation); position = lerp(scatterPos, gridPos, assembleEase(phase)) so they fly in from scattered to the flat grid (or out, per direction); opacity rises. Controls: duration (fader), gridN (knob 4..12 -> resolution), scatter (fader 1..6 scatter radius). Deterministic (index hash, no Math.random). Observable: a voxel's position changes across phase, converging to its grid slot. Dispose the instanced/group geometry+material; restore subject. DISTINCT from crumble (gravity fall) / shatter.

F.name: gravity-drop
F.label: Gravity Drop
F.subject: empty
F.description: A burst of particles drops under gravity and bounces off an invisible floor, energy damping with each hit — deterministic physics.
F.behavior: subject:'empty' — build your own THREE.Points/Group into target.object. N particles each with a deterministic initial position+velocity from an index hash (fract(sin(i*12.9898)*43758.5453)). In seek integrate analytically or step: y(t) with gravity and floor bounces (reflect velocity * restitution at y=floor), x drifts linearly. Update geometry.attributes.position; needsUpdate=true. Controls: gravity (knob), restitution (fader 0.2..0.9 bounciness), count (knob 60..400). DETERMINISTIC only. Observable: a particle's y decreases then bounces (a position-array element changes across two t). Dispose geometry+material. DISTINCT from rain/fountain (no floor bounce).

F.name: explosion
F.label: Explosion
F.subject: empty
F.description: A particle explosion bursts outward from the center in all directions, decelerating and fading like a firework shell.
F.behavior: subject:'empty' — build THREE.Points into target.object. N particles each get a deterministic unit direction from an index hash (spherical distribution via hashed angles) and a speed. In seek position = dir * speed * easeOutBurst(t) (fast then decelerating, e.g. 1-exp(-k*t)) + slight gravity on y; size/opacity fade with t. Update position attribute. Controls: power (knob burst speed), gravity (fader 0..2), count (knob 80..500). DETERMINISTIC. Observable: a particle's radial distance grows then plateaus. Dispose. DISTINCT from confetti (gravity confetti) / sparks.

G.name: light-sweep
G.label: Light Sweep
G.subject: card
G.description: A bright specular band sweeps diagonally across the card surface, like light glancing off glossy plastic.
G.behavior: TSL: swap subject.material to a MeshStandardNodeMaterial; emissiveNode adds a moving diagonal band: b = smoothstep(width,0, abs(dot(uv, dir) - uSweep)); emissive += tint * b * intensity. seek advances uSweep across the surface (loop or one-shot). Use three/tsl (uv, dot, abs, smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), width (knob 0.04..0.4), angleDeg (knob -> dir). Track uSweep.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from holographic (rainbow foil) / metallic-sheen — a single clean specular band.

G.name: caustic-shimmer
G.label: Caustic Shimmer
G.subject: card
G.description: Soft refracted light caustics shimmer over the card surface, like sunlight through water dancing on a wall.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial; emissiveNode adds a caustic pattern = pow(abs(sin(uv.x*f + uTime) + sin(uv.y*f - uTime*1.3) + sin((uv.x+uv.y)*f*0.7 + uTime*0.6)), sharp) * tint * intensity (a cheap moving interference caustic). seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), scale (knob f 4..16), intensity (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from caustics-ripple/underwater-caustics (those distort/overlay on a plane) — this is a soft additive shimmer over a card surface, shimmer-category.

G.name: prism-spectrum
G.label: Prism Spectrum
G.subject: card
G.description: A rolling spectral rainbow refraction sweeps across the surface — white light split into a moving prism spectrum.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial; colorNode or emissiveNode = a spectrum mapped from a moving coordinate: s = fract(dot(uv,dir)*bands - uTime*speed); spectralColor(s) via a hue->rgb (e.g. cos-palette: 0.5+0.5*cos(6.283*(s + vec3(0,0.33,0.67)))) scaled by intensity, added to base. seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl (uv, dot, fract, cos, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), bands (knob 1..6), intensity (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from iridescence (fresnel oil-slick) / holographic — explicit moving spectral bands.

G.name: glint-streak
G.label: Glint Streak
G.subject: card
G.description: Sharp anamorphic glints flare across bright points of the card — crisp lens-flare streaks that twinkle and travel.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial; emissiveNode adds anamorphic star streaks at moving hotspots: for a hotspot at uHot (animated), streak = intensity * (exp(-abs(uv.x-uHot.x)*kx*ky_for_vertical) ... ) — a cross/horizontal streak kernel; plus a twinkle = (0.5+0.5*sin(uTime*tw)). seek advances uTime/uHot. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), length (knob streak length), intensity (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from sparkle-glints (point sparkles) — these are long anamorphic streaks.

G.name: pearlescent
G.label: Pearlescent
G.subject: card
G.description: A soft pearlescent sheen shifts hue across the surface with view angle, like mother-of-pearl — pastel, low-contrast, premium.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial; use a fresnel-like term (based on normal/view or a uv gradient proxy) to drive a pastel hue shift: f = pow(1 - abs(uv.y-0.5)*2, power) (proxy fresnel); hue = base + f*range + uTime*drift; color = mix(base, pastelPalette(hue), sheen). seek advances uTime slowly. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: drift (knob slow), range (knob hue spread), sheen (fader 0..1). Keep PASTEL/low-contrast (premium, not neon). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from iridescence (oil-slick saturated) — pearl is soft pastel.

G.name: chromatic-aberration
G.label: Chromatic Glass
G.subject: card
G.description: Transmissive glass with strong chromatic aberration — RGB channels split at the refracted edges into colored fringes.
G.behavior: TSL: swap subject.material to MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial (three/webgpu) with transmission=1, thickness, ior, roughness low; drive a per-channel ior/dispersion via the material's dispersion property (if available) OR approximate edge fringe via an emissiveNode rim that splits RGB by a uDispersion uniform; animate ior/dispersion subtly with uTime. Use three/tsl and CAST node assignments like caustics.ts; keep prevMat and restore in dispose. Controls: ior (fader 1.1..2.0), dispersion (knob 0..1 fringe strength), thickness (fader 0.1..3). Track a uniform (ior/dispersion) .value as observable. flagRealGpu=true (transmission under-renders headless). DISTINCT from existing 'dispersion' — this is physical-transmission RGB fringing.

G.name: bevel-glass
G.label: Beveled Glass
G.subject: card
G.description: A thick beveled-edge glass panel — chunky refraction concentrated at chamfered borders with a clear center.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial with transmission=1, high thickness, low roughness; build a normalNode that tilts toward the edges (a beveled normal: near the uv borders push the normal outward, flat in the center) so refraction concentrates at the bevel. Animate a faint thickness/uTime shimmer. Use three/tsl (uv, normal manipulation, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: bevel (knob 0.05..0.4 edge width), thickness (fader), ior (fader 1.2..1.9). Track a uniform .value. flagRealGpu=true. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from frosted/liquid/crystal glass — beveled-edge refraction.

G.name: water-droplet
G.label: Water Droplet
G.subject: sphere
G.description: A clear water droplet lens — high-transmission sphere that magnifies and refracts what's behind it, with a moving surface tension wobble.
G.behavior: TSL: subject is a sphere; swap to MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial transmission=1, ior~1.33 (water), thickness, roughness 0; add a subtle positionNode or normal wobble = sin(position*f + uTime)*amp to simulate surface tension jiggle. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: ior (fader 1.2..1.5), wobble (knob 0..0.1), thickness (fader). Track a uniform .value. flagRealGpu=true. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT — water droplet on a sphere subject, surface-tension wobble.

G.name: ice-glass
G.label: Ice Glass
G.subject: card
G.description: Frosted crystalline ice — semi-transmissive with a cracked/faceted frozen normal and a cold blue tint, frost creeping over time.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial, transmission ~0.85, roughness mid (frosty), thickness; normalNode perturbed by a faceted/cellular crack noise (voronoi-ish or layered sin) for the ice crystal facets; a cold blue attenuationColor/tint; animate a uFrost uniform that grows the roughness/crack density over time (frost creeping). Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: frost (fader 0..1 -> roughness+crack), tint (color default cold blue), thickness (fader). Track uFrost.value. flagRealGpu=true. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from frosted-glass (smooth frost) — ice has crystalline crack facets.

G.name: pool-caustics
G.label: Pool Caustics
G.subject: plane
G.description: Bright caustic light-net dances on a pool floor — sharp interfering light cells crawling across the plane.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial on the plane; colorNode/emissiveNode = caustic cells: build a cellular pattern e.g. c = pow(1 - voronoiDist(uv*scale + flow(uTime)), sharp) summed over 2 layers moving in different directions; tint sunlit. seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl (uv, sin/cellular noise, pow, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), scale (knob 3..14), sharpness (knob 1..6 cell contrast). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from caustics-ripple (ripple-distort) and underwater-caustics — this is a sharp pool-floor light net.

G.name: caustic-net
G.label: Caustic Net
G.subject: plane
G.description: A flowing web of caustic filaments — thin bright threads of light weaving and drifting like reflections off rippled water.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshStandardNodeMaterial on the plane; emissiveNode = thin filament net: f = abs(sin(uv.x*a + uTime) * sin(uv.y*b - uTime*1.2) + sin((uv.x-uv.y)*c + uTime*0.7)); net = pow(1 - clamp(f,0,1), thinPow) (thin bright lines where f~0); tint. seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob), density (knob a/b/c scale), thinness (knob thinPow 2..8). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from pool-caustics (cells) — net is thin filament threads.

G.name: ink-bloom
G.label: Ink Bloom
G.subject: plane
G.description: A drop of ink blooms into water — a dark organic cloud unfurling and diffusing outward with feathered tendrils.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshBasicNodeMaterial (or Standard) on the plane; colorNode/opacityNode = an ink cloud: d = length(uv-0.5); density = smoothstep(uGrow, uGrow-edge, d + fbmNoise(uv*scale + uTime*flow)*wobble) (a growing feathered blob); color dark ink tint, alpha = density. seek advances uGrow 0->~0.9 and uTime (turbulent unfurl). Use three/tsl (uv, length, fbm/sin noise, smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob bloom rate), turbulence (knob wobble), scale (knob noise). Track uGrow.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from ink-spread (existing) — ink-bloom is a center-out turbulent diffusing cloud with feathered tendrils, smoke-category fluid.

G.name: smoke-plume
G.label: Smoke Plume
G.subject: plane
G.description: A turbulent smoke plume rises and curls upward, billowing wider as it ascends and dissipates at the top.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshBasicNodeMaterial on the plane; opacityNode/colorNode = rising plume: sample fbm noise advected upward (uv.y - uTime*rise) with horizontal curl (uv.x + sin(uv.y*curlFreq + uTime)*curl); density masked by a vertical envelope (wider+fainter toward top). seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl (uv, fbm/layered sin noise, smoothstep, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: rise (knob speed), curl (knob horizontal swirl), density (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from wispy-smoke/steam — directed rising curling plume with a vertical dissipation envelope.

G.name: dust-cloud
G.label: Dust Cloud
G.subject: plane
G.description: A drifting cloud of fine dust catches light — soft low-density haze slowly billowing sideways with motes glinting.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshBasicNodeMaterial on the plane; opacityNode = low-density drifting haze: fbm(uv*scale + vec2(uTime*driftX, uTime*driftY*0.3)) thresholded soft (low alpha); colorNode warm dusty tint with a faint sparkle term (high-freq noise) for motes. seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: drift (knob speed), density (fader 0..0.6 keep low/hazy), scale (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from clouds (volumetric)/fog — thin drifting dust haze with glinting motes.

G.name: campfire
G.label: Campfire
G.subject: plane
G.description: A small flickering campfire — licking orange-to-yellow flame tongues with a hot core and rising sparks, warmer and tighter than the big fire.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshBasicNodeMaterial on the plane; colorNode = flame: a vertical flame mask m = smoothstep(0, 1, flameProfile(uv, uTime)) where flameProfile uses upward-advected noise (uv.y - uTime) modulated by a centered horizontal envelope that narrows toward the top (tongue shape); palette ramps blackbody hot-core -> yellow -> orange -> dark by height/intensity; opacityNode = m. seek advances uTime (flicker). Use three/tsl (uv, layered sin/fbm noise, smoothstep, mix, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob flicker), height (knob flame length), intensity (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from fire-flame — campfire is a tighter, warmer, multi-tongue blackbody flame.

G.name: aurora
G.label: Aurora
G.subject: plane
G.description: Aurora borealis curtains — vertical ribbons of green-to-violet light waving and shimmering across a night sky.
G.behavior: TSL: MeshBasicNodeMaterial on the plane; colorNode = aurora curtains: vertical ribbons whose horizontal position waves with uv.y and uTime: ribbon = exp(-pow((uv.x - curtainPath(uv.y, uTime))/width, 2)); intensity falls off with height; palette mixes green->teal->violet by uv.y and a slow uTime hue drift; sum 2-3 curtains. opacityNode = total intensity. seek advances uTime. Use three/tsl (uv, sin, exp, mix, uniform) and CAST like caustics.ts. Controls: speed (knob wave), width (knob ribbon width), brightness (knob). Track uTime.value. Restore prevMat in dispose. DISTINCT from nebula/plasma — structured vertical waving curtains.

G.name: swarm
G.label: Swarm
G.subject: empty
G.description: A swarm of particles flows along a curling field toward a drifting attractor, like a school of fish or a flock reorganizing.
G.behavior: subject:'empty' — build THREE.Points into target.object. N particles with deterministic initial positions (index hash). In seek, move each particle along a curl/flow field: velocity from a deterministic curl-noise of (position, uTime) plus attraction toward a slowly drifting attractor point (a function of uTime); integrate position with small dt per seek BUT keep deterministic & reproducible — derive position purely as a function of (i, t) so reseeking the same t is identical (e.g. position(i,t) = basePath(i) + curlField(i, t)). Update position attribute. Controls: speed (knob), cohesion (knob attractor pull), spread (fader). DETERMINISTIC (index hash, no Math.random, position is a pure function of i and t). Observable: a particle position element changes across two t. Dispose. DISTINCT from existing particle fields.

G.name: flocking
G.label: Flocking
G.subject: empty
G.description: Particles flock in a coherent flowing band, aligning direction and sweeping across the field like starlings at dusk.
G.behavior: subject:'empty' — THREE.Points. N particles arranged into a flowing band whose centerline migrates with uTime; each particle's position is a pure function of (i, t): a base lane offset (from index hash) + a shared flow advection (sin fields) so the whole group moves coherently with local variation (alignment look). Update position attribute. Controls: speed (knob), alignment (knob -> how tightly they share the flow vs individual offset), count (knob 100..600). DETERMINISTIC pure-function-of-(i,t). Observable: positions change across t and the group stays coherent. Dispose. DISTINCT from swarm (attractor convergence) — flocking is a coherent migrating band.

G.name: attractor
G.label: Strange Attractor
G.subject: empty
G.description: Particles trace a strange attractor — points distributed along a Lorenz/Aizawa orbit, the whole structure slowly rotating in space.
G.behavior: subject:'empty' — THREE.Points. Precompute (deterministically, once at build) N points along a strange-attractor orbit by iterating the Aizawa or Lorenz map from a fixed seed (NO Math.random — fixed initial state + fixed params), scaled to fit. In seek, rotate the whole point cloud (rotation.y/x = t*speed) and optionally pulse scale; the attractor shape is static, the cloud revolves. Update via object rotation (cheap) — but ALSO ensure a position-array or rotation observable changes. Controls: speed (knob rotation), variant (dropdown lorenz|aizawa), scale (fader). DETERMINISTIC. Observable: object.rotation changes across t (assert rotation, or a transformed point). Dispose geometry+material. DISTINCT — mathematical attractor structure.

G.name: morph-cloud
G.label: Morph Cloud
G.subject: empty
G.description: A point cloud morphs between two shapes — sphere to cube to torus and back — particles smoothly interpolating between target sets.
G.behavior: subject:'empty' — THREE.Points. Precompute (deterministic) two or three target position sets for the same N particles (e.g. a sphere via index-hash spherical distribution, a cube via hashed face positions, a torus). In seek, blend = a triangle/sine of t cycling 0..1..0 between shape A and B (and a phase selecting which pair); position[i] = lerp(targetA[i], targetB[i], smoothstep(blend)). Update position attribute. Controls: speed (knob morph rate), shapes (dropdown sphere-cube|sphere-torus|cube-torus), jitter (knob small noise). DETERMINISTIC (index hash). Observable: a particle position element changes across t as shapes blend. Dispose. DISTINCT — explicit shape interpolation.

G.name: vortex
G.label: Vortex
G.subject: empty
G.description: Particles spiral inward into a glowing vortex, accelerating as they near the eye then recycling outward — a continuous whirlpool.
G.behavior: subject:'empty' — THREE.Points. Each particle i has a deterministic base radius and angle (index hash). In seek, angle = baseAngle + t*swirlSpeed/(radius+eps) (inner spins faster); radius = recycle(baseRadius - t*inflow mod range) so particles spiral inward and recycle outward continuously; map to x,z (or x,y) with a slight y bob. Update position attribute. Controls: swirl (knob angular speed), inflow (knob radial pull), count (knob 100..500). DETERMINISTIC. Observable: a particle's angle/position changes across t (inner faster than outer). Dispose. DISTINCT from fountain/explosion — inward spiral whirlpool.
